picks.excerpt: Microsoft moved for summary judgment on 4 September in the consolidated copyright litigation brought by book authors and news publishers, telling a federal court that Copilot almost never reproduces books verbatim.
picks.rationale: Microsoft's own summary-judgment filing puts a number on how often Copilot regurgitates books — the defense argument that will shape what publishers can claim next.

picks.excerpt: 404 Media follows up its Amazon book-destruction investigation with a worker who slices spines off printed books so they can be scanned for AI training.
picks.rationale: First-hand account from inside the scanning line turns the abstract 'books as training data' debate into a physical, documented supply chain.

picks.excerpt: TCL's P80 Pro and P80 Ultra convert e-books into AI-narrated audiobooks or podcast-style summaries on-device, and add a hardware key that drops the phone into a paper-like e-reader mode.
picks.rationale: On-device book-to-audio conversion shipping in a mainstream phone moves AI narration out of publisher pipelines and into the reader's hand.

picks.excerpt: A new Public Library Quarterly article, 'Accountability, Integrity: AI Policy in Public Libraries,' examines how U.S. public libraries are actually writing generative-AI policy for staff and patrons.
picks.rationale: A researched look at the generative-AI policies public libraries are actually adopting — a template for any institution drafting its own rules.

picks.rationale: Korea's biggest reading subscription lays out five concrete directions for AI-era reading experience — a product roadmap, not a think piece.
